title: 10 Odd Town Festivals
summary: Josh and Chuck tour unusual town festivals around the world, opening with the punkin chunkin contest in Sussex County, Delaware (a St. Jude's benefit with air cannons, centrifuges and catapults). They cover Frozen Dead Guy Days in Nederland, Colorado; the Rocky Mountain Oyster Festival in Clinton, Montana and the Throckmorton, Texas version; the Festival of Near Death Experiences in Santa Marta de Retortillo, Spain; the World Wife Carrying Championships in Sonkajärvi, Finland; La Tomatina in Buñol, Spain; and the Amtrak mooning party in Laguna Niguel, California. The episode closes with a listener email from Natalie in Massachusetts about listening during silent study at boarding school.
topics: St. Jude's Children's Research Hospital benefit

segments.title: Opening banter and punkin chunkin
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter about punkin chunkin and the Science Channel show, then discuss the Delaware pumpkin-launching contest benefiting St. Jude's, its air cannon, centrifuge and catapult categories, and the world distance record.

segments.title: Frozen Dead Guy Days
segments.summary: Chuck describes Frozen Dead Guy Days in Nederland, Colorado, a March festival built around Grandpa Bredo Morstøl, cryogenically preserved after dying in 1989 and later returned to a shed. Events include coffin races, salmon tossing, frozen beach volleyball and a polar plunge.

segments.title: Rocky Mountain Oyster Festival
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the September Testicle Festival in Clinton, Montana, known as the Rocky Mountain Oyster Festival, with about ten thousand attendees eating bull testicles, plus contests and events. They also mention the similar Throckmorton, Texas festival and its taste-like-chicken cook-off.

segments.title: Festival of Near Death Experiences
segments.summary: Hosts describe the July festival in Santa Marta de Retortillo, Spain, where people who had near death experiences are carried into church in coffins to tell their stories.

segments.title: World Wife Carrying Championships
segments.summary: The hosts cover the wife carrying race in Sonkajärvi, Finland, including the weight rules, the prize of beer equal to the wife's weight, the Estonian carrying method, and the 2009 winners.

segments.title: La Tomatina
segments.summary: The hosts describe the tomato fight in Buñol, Spain, held for an hour on the last Wednesday of August, starting in 1945 with uncertain origins, with about 140 tons of tomatoes.

segments.title: Amtrak mooning party in Laguna Niguel
segments.summary: The hosts describe an annual July mooning of passing Amtrak trains in Laguna Niguel, California, begun around 1980 with no organizers, and how police keep it peaceful. Chuck shares a story of mooning girls while a sixth-grade crossing guard.

segments.title: Listener email from Natalie
segments.summary: Natalie, a boarding school student in Massachusetts, writes that she listens during silent study, shared an MK Ultra fact with her English class, and asks for a shout-out.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Hosts plug the HowStuffWorks site and sign off.
